title: Home decisions, compared with your numbers
description: Compare UK mortgages, deposits, renting, buying and moving. See monthly payments, upfront costs, interest and equity side by side.

title: Mortgage decisions
description: Compare rates, fees, terms and overpayments. Keep both the monthly budget and the debt left at the end in view.

title: Buying a home
description: Compare the cash needed to buy with the long-term cost of owning. Explore deposit choices and renting on equal budgets.

title: Moving or improving
description: Start with your existing equity. Compare transaction costs, borrowing, building work and what you may own afterwards.

title: Find your comparison
description: Sixteen tools for UK home and property decisions. Choose a question, replace the illustrative figures and compare both paths.

title: Understand the numbers
description: Practical explanations of the costs, assumptions and trade-offs behind a home decision.

title: Real numbers. Worked through.
description: Eight focused illustrations show how a change in fees, rates, terms or deposits can alter a comparison.

description: Test whether interest savings repay a quoted early repayment charge and switching costs.

title: Rent vs buy calculator

title: 5% vs 10% deposit calculator
description: Compare borrowing costs and the cash tied up in a larger deposit.

title: 10% vs 20% deposit calculator
description: See how a larger cash commitment changes interest, payments and equity.

title: How mortgage interest actually works
description: A repayment mortgage pays both interest and principal. The split changes even when the payment stays the same.

title: How product fees change the real mortgage cost
description: A cheaper rate can come with a larger fixed cost. The balance and the time you keep the deal determine whether it pays back.

title: What mortgage break-even means
description: Break-even is a crossing between two cost paths. Define the costs before relying on the date.

title: How early repayment charges work
description: An early repayment charge can change the economics of switching even when the new rate is lower.

title: How mortgage overpayments affect interest
description: Overpayments reduce principal sooner. Keeping the ordinary payment unchanged can shorten the mortgage.

title: Should you choose a shorter mortgage term?
description: A shorter term increases the required payment and usually reduces interest under the same rate.

title: Costs people forget when moving house
description: A price gap is only part of a moving budget. Selling, buying and the overlap between homes create separate bills.

title: Costs people forget when buying a home
description: The deposit is only one part of the cash required. Build a budget for completion and for the first year.

title: How deposit size affects a mortgage
description: A larger deposit reduces borrowing. A rate reduction may provide a second benefit, but it needs a real quote.

title: Understanding loan-to-value
description: Loan-to-value expresses the mortgage as a percentage of the property value used by the lender.

title: How to compare mortgage deals properly
description: Keep the starting balance, time horizon and repayment basis consistent before comparing rates.

title: What happens when a fixed mortgage ends?
description: The fixed rate has an end date; the mortgage balance usually has many more years to run.

title: How to estimate the cost of extending a house
description: An extension budget needs a scope, quotes and a contingency before a financial comparison becomes meaningful.

title: How to compare moving with improving your home
description: Both routes can buy a better living arrangement, but the financial paths and practical trade-offs differ.

title: What costs are involved in downsizing?
description: A cheaper replacement home may release equity, but the amount available is lower than the headline price gap.

title: Is a £999 mortgage fee worth it?
description: A two-year deal gives a fixed fee little time to repay itself. Compare a smaller balance too: the fee stays £999 while the interest saving shrinks.

title: When does a £1,499 mortgage fee pay back?
description: A higher fee on a smaller balance is a useful stress test. The rate gap alone does not tell you whether this product earns its fee within two years.

title: 4% vs 5% on a £200,000 mortgage
description: This isolates a one-percentage-point rate difference with no switching fees. Add an actual fee or ERC before using it to assess a real remortgage.

title: £200,000 mortgage: 25 vs 30 years
description: Five extra years reduce the contractual payment but leave more debt after five years. The balance row measures the part of the payment reduction that has simply been postponed.

title: £250,000 mortgage: 25 vs 35 years
description: A ten-year extension has a visible monthly benefit and a long interest tail. Compare the full-term figure with the shorter five-year debt snapshot rather than treating either alone as the answer.

title: What does a £200 monthly overpayment change?
description: The comparison gives the saver the same £200 each month. Mortgage interest avoided and savings interest earned are both counted, while access to the cash remains a separate consideration.

title: A £500 monthly overpayment versus saving
description: A ten-year view makes the compounding effect visible. Check the lender’s allowance before assuming that £6,000 of extra payments each year is penalty-free.

title: 5% vs 10% deposit on a £200,000 home
description: The extra £10,000 reduces borrowing and changes the assumed rate. This is a same-day choice: it excludes the rent and price changes involved in waiting to save. Property tax is excluded from this illustration and must be entered for a real purchase.
